overview: Explore top accredited institutions, tuition costs, eligibility, and visa procedures in Denmark for Mechanical Engineering (UG) in Denmark.

universities.name: Technical University of Denmark (DTU)
universities.desc: The Technical University of Denmark is a leading university with a clear focus on engineering, technology, innovation and research. Students should consult the current list of bachelor's programs and language requirements.

universities.name: Aarhus University
universities.desc: Aarhus University provides education in engineering, technology and related science and technology subjects. Students may pursue appropriate academic pathways according to their interests.

universities.name: University of Southern Denmark (SDU)
universities.desc: The University of Southern Denmark offers engineering programs and technology-oriented disciplines. SDU offers a BEng in Mechanical Engineering in English in Sønderborg. The program is based on practical projects and an internship.

universities.name: Aalborg University (AAU)
universities.desc: Aalborg University is well known for its problem-based learning approach and engineering education. Students who are interested in practical engineering and project-based learning can explore its relevant programs.

universities.name: VIA University College
universities.desc: VIA University College offers education within applied engineering, including professional programs within engineering. It has a Mechanical Engineering bachelor's program in Horsens with a focus on product development and design. Students should check the language and current intake before applying. Important: These institutions are suggestions to consider, not a confirmation that each currently offers an English-taught bachelor's degree specifically called Mechanical Engineering. Always check the exact program and intake before applying. Edu-Hawk Worldwide can help students compare available study options and understand the application process.

items.q: How Long Does It Take to Get a Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering in Denmark?
items.a: A standard bachelor's degree is three years, but a professional Bachelor of Engineering degree is usually 3.5 years and may include an internship. How long it takes to complete depends on the university and program you choose.

items.q: Can Indian Students Study Mechanical Engineering in English in Denmark?
items.a: Yes. For example, the University of Southern Denmark offers a BEng in Mechanical Engineering, taught in English, in Sønderborg. Students should check with the program to verify current availability and admission requirements prior to application.

items.q: What Will Be the Cost Per Year?
items.a: The first-year budget is around ₹20 lakh–₹32 lakh, including tuition and living expenses. Check the actual university fees and calculate your own living expenses before applying.

items.q: Do You Need Mathematics to Get In?
items.a: Mathematics is often one of the key admission subjects for mechanical engineering. Physics and sometimes Chemistry may also be required, depending on the program.

items.q: Is It Possible to Do a Master's After Completing My Bachelor's?
items.a: Yes. Depending on your degree, academic performance and prerequisite subjects, you may be eligible to apply for a relevant master's program in mechanical engineering or a related field.
